It's been just over a year since OpenAI launched its first GPT-5 model for use in ChatGPT. Now it's time for GPT-6 Astra to upgrade ChatGPT and Codex capabilities. Details below.

GPT-6 Astra Details

OpenAI officially introduced its new model, GPT-6 Astra, describing it as "the world's smartest, most aligned model."

Here's more from today's official announcement:

OpenAI further detailed how GPT-6 improves computer control capabilities, allowing ChatGPT to operate while you're using a Mac or other desktop computer, including running in the background while you work:

Additionally, OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra is "the best model for software engineering to date."

As for Codex, here are some new capabilities GPT-6 brings:

OpenAI called GPT-6 Astra a "significant leap in cybersecurity capabilities," noting it "hits a critical cybersecurity threshold under the Preparedness Framework."

As a result, the model is rolling out slowly to users.

OpenAI stated: "GPT‑6 Astra begins rolling out today to a limited number of organizations, and will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the coming days, and via the OpenAI API and AWS."

"Astra usage counts against existing subscription quotas, and users and businesses can also purchase additional usage credits. Pro, Business, and Enterprise plan users will have access to GPT‑6 Astra Pro. Enterprise administrators can enable Astra for their workspaces; it will be off by default at launch."

GPT-6 Astra Background

GPT-5 launched on August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and several reasoning models to become the default model in ChatGPT. Its signature feature was automatic routing: ChatGPT could provide quick answers or engage deeper reasoning based on the request. OpenAI also claimed it had fewer factual errors than GPT-4o.

Apple adopted the model in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests processed through Apple Intelligence—including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence—were switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5.

GPT-5.1 brought warmer, more natural responses in November. The "red alert" GPT-5.2 in December accelerated professional workflows in response to Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant adjusted ChatGPT's "cringe" tone, and two days later GPT-5.4 Thinking launched with a million-token context window and built-in computer control capabilities.

OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for greater autonomy, GPT-5.5 Instant, and the July GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models.

From the Codex Mac App to the New ChatGPT

The software surrounding these models also went through transformations. In February, OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app as a central platform for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling tasks.

In July, Codex essentially became the new ChatGPT desktop app, integrating Chat, Work, and Codex, while the original native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

For me, Codex fundamentally changed how I use ChatGPT. I can outsource more work that doesn't require intense focus, and even build tools on my Mac that I couldn't before.

GPT-6 Availability

OpenAI said the new GPT-6 model will initially only be available to members of its cybersecurity-focused Daybreak program. This is similar to the previous release cadence of GPT-5.6.
